scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for the person to delete their stepbrother's profile on their Nintendo Switch. Let me break this down step by step. First, the scenario: The person had to watch their stepbrother for a week. They brought their Switch to pass the time on the train. The stepbrother wanted to play, so they created a new profile for him to keep their saves safe. That seems reasonable because it prevented any accidental overwrites or mess-ups of their own games. During that week, the stepbrother was really into playing, which helped distract him while the person studied. So, the profile was useful for both of them. It kept the stepbrother entertained and allowed the person to focus on their studies without worrying about their games being messed up. After the week was over, the person went back to school. They found it annoying to have to switch profiles every time they wanted to play a game or go to the eShop. So, they decided to delete the stepbrother's profile. That seems like a minor inconvenience for them, but maybe they didn't consider how it would affect the stepbrother. Fast forward to Thanksgiving, the person brings the Switch again. The stepbrother starts playing and realizes his Zelda save is gone. He gets upset, cries a little, and now is upset. The dad thinks it was mean to delete the profile because the stepbrother was enjoying it. So, the question is: Was it right or wrong to delete the profile? Let me think about the factors involved. The person created the profile to help manage their own games, which is a good thing. They were accommodating the stepbrother's interest in gaming, which helped during the week. However, after the week, they felt annoyed by the extra step of switching profiles. So, they took action to make it easier for themselves. But by deleting the profile, they removed the stepbrother's progress and access to the games. The stepbrother was emotionally affected, which shows that the profile meant something to him. The dad's reaction also indicates that it was seen as a mean action. So, considering the impact on the stepbrother, it seems like the person didn't think about how their action would affect him. They focused on their own convenience without considering the emotional investment the stepbrother had in the games. In terms of right or wrong, it's more about the consideration for others' feelings. Deleting the profile without discussing it or giving the stepbrother a chance to save his progress was probably not the best move. It shows a lack of empathy and consideration for the stepbrother's enjoyment and effort in the games. Therefore, it was wrong because it disregarded the stepbrother's feelings and investment in the games, leading to emotional distress.
